column1: # Dataset: Business Survivability Scores by Neighborhood - Seattle (2026)
# Description: Predicted probability (0-100%) that a business type survives 2+ years at neighborhood level in Seattle
# Scores are based on 100+ location factors and 570
column2: 000+ real business outcomes across 24 US metros

column1: # Scale: projected chance of lasting two or more years
column3: calibrated per sector; never the model's raw output

column1: # Note: This file carries one row per business type and place. Its score is the projected chance of lasting two or more years
column2: averaged across the price points StreetSpring scores separately in the tool (most types have 5). The 110 business types here are base types; the tool offers 500+ business types
column3: counting each type at each of its price points.

column1: # Business types: StreetSpring scores 500+ business types: 153 base business types
column2: most of them at 5 price points
column3: which is 569 type-and-price combinations you can choose in the tool.

column1: # Columns: city = Metro slug (for example philadelphia).; neighborhood = Neighborhood slug inside the metro; the row's place.; business_subtype = Business type slug (for example italian-restaurant); the row's business. The file's own count is in the README and on its page.; business_type_lookup = Display name of the business type (for example Italian Restaurant).; avg_survivability_score = The headline number: the projected chance
column3: that this business type lasts two or more years at a typical address in this neighborhood. Use this column to answer 'where should I open X'.; max_survivability_score = Best address in the neighborhood for this business type
column4: 0 to 100.; the rest are in the README; neighborhood_overall_score = Mean p90_survivability_score of the place's ranked business types.; neighborhood_overall_avg_score = Mean avg_survivability_score of the same rows.; neighborhood_overall_max_score = Mean max_survivability_score of the same rows.; neighborhood_overall_min_score = Mean min_survivability_score of the same rows.; business_types_ranked_in_neighborhood = How many business types are ranked in the place.; neighborhood_overall_rank = The place's rank among places of the same kind on neighborhood_overall_score (1 = best).; total_ranked_neighborhoods_overall = Size of that list.

column1: # Ranking: rows are ranked on p90_survivability_score
column2: the score at a good address (90th percentile of the scored locations inside the place)
column3: NOT on the average. Ranking a place by its average ranks how uniform it is
column4: not how good its best locations are.

column1: # Place kinds: city neighbourhoods and whole municipalities are ranked in SEPARATE lists. place_kind says which. A rank is only ever against places of the same kind
column2: and total_ranked_neighborhoods_for_business_subtype is the size of that kind's list
column3: which can be fewer than ten.

column1: # Not every place is ranked: a place needs at least 10 scored locations of its own and at least 5 peer places of the same kind. Unranked places keep their score and their page; the rank
column2: tier and list-size columns are empty for them.

column1: # Not every business type is ranked: the rank
column2: tier and overall columns cover the business types StreetSpring publishes guides for. The other scored types keep their scores with empty rank columns.
Where should I open a given business in this metro? Filter business_subtype to the type AND place_kind to the kind you want
column3: sort by p90_survivability_score descending (or neighborhood_rank_for_business_subtype ascending

How do two places compare for the same business? Compare p90_survivability_score for the best-address view and avg_survivability_score for the typical-address view. Only compare places with the same place_kind.

column1: # Overall rank: neighborhood_overall_rank ranks the place against places of the same kind on neighborhood_overall_score
column2: the mean p90_survivability_score of its ranked business types; ties break on the mean average
column3: then scored locations. The four neighborhood_overall_* scores are means over the same ranked rows.

column2: Which neighborhoods are strongest overall? Filter place_kind
column3: sort by neighborhood_overall_rank ascending; the file has one row per business type
column4: so drop duplicates on neighborhood first.
